key_insight: A quantum convolutional neural network can act as a compact surrogate model for predicting groundwater heat plume behavior, with performance that improves when error mitigation is applied.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a path toward faster geothermal groundwater temperature forecasting using quantum-enhanced models when full-scale simulations are too expensive or too high-dimensional.
method: Reduce high-dimensional simulation outputs to a small set of representative target parameters.
Use a QCNN with quantum convolution, quantum pooling, and a quantum readout stage.
Encode inputs with a Hamiltonian-inspired feature map and test on simulators and IBM hardware.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated with mean squared error on training and test sets across an ideal simulator, a noisy simulator, IBM's 127-qubit Kyiv device, and error-mitigated hardware runs.
watch_item: The approach still depends on reduced surrogate targets and current quantum hardware noise, so it is not yet a replacement for full classical predictive accuracy.
paper_title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Groundwater Heat Plume Prediction: A Surrogate Modeling Approach
